designs.title: Vitis vinifera
designs.why: Clean, very printable one-ink plate: 12% coverage, no strokes under ~0.3 mm, no specks, open counters, captions big enough to hold on a 230-mesh screen. It reads well on white from 3 m. Up close at full size the contours wobble and bead the way auto-traced scans do, and the leaf hatching breaks into scattered dashes. That cheapens it next to a real engraved plate. The pruned cane floats off on the right, which leaves the layout lopsided.
designs.fix: Redraw or smooth the outlines and hatching into steady, tapered, continuous strokes (no beaded edges, no broken dash fields). Then pull the pruned cane in closer so the plate sits as one balanced block.

designs.title: Fermentation
designs.why: Strong subject and composition. The tank linework and valve hardware are crisp, the labels are clean serif type at a holdable size, and coverage is a light 9%. On a black tee in white ink, the near-solid bubble field along the tank walls and the yeast-in-suspension band will gain and fill into flat blobs. At chest size the labels go illegible from a distance. There are also a few stray ticks and specks, for example one beside the cone on the right, and the Kräusen umlaut renders oddly.
designs.fix: Separate it for white-on-black: choke the dense bubble and wall-shading zones open by about 0.1-0.15 mm so they don't fill in under white ink. While doing that, remove the stray marks and fix the ä glyph.

designs.title: Shaping
designs.why: At full size this is a thresholded photo, not drawn art. Every tone is broken, wormy noise, the board and blank outlines are dashed and unclosed, and coverage is heavy (27%), with lots of hairline paper gaps in the textured areas. Those gaps will fill and mottle on press and give a stiff, blotchy hand. It reads at 3 m, but up close it looks like a cheap photocopy for a $50 shirt. The mono SHAPING header is fine.
designs.fix: Redraw the figure as deliberate line-and-hatch illustration: closed board outline, controlled hatching instead of threshold noise, and large dark areas opened up. That brings coverage under about 18% and removes the fine gaps that will plug.
